title: Australia trimmed mean CPI rises to 3.7%, above forecasts, as RBA hike case firms
body: Oil is the clearest driver of the headline beat, and Bullock tied higher energy prices directly to a worse inflation outlook only minutes before the release, so any further rise in crude adds to the case for tightening. The bigger signal for markets is the core reading. A trimmed mean that rose to 3.7%, when the RBA had expected it to stabilise, supports pricing for a hike on November 2 and 3, and backs the Australian dollar and front-end yields. The slightly softer weighted median takes a little off that, but not enough to change the overall message. AUD/NZD traders also face the RBNZ decision at 01:00 GMT, where a widely expected hike could limit any relative move in the Aussie. --- Earlier: RBA's Bullock: oil shock means inflation above August forecasts, Board meets next week --- Australia's core inflation picked up instead of levelling off, landing just as Governor Bullock was telling senators that inflation is running above the RBA's forecasts. Summary: Q3 trimmed mean CPI rose 1.0% q/q (expected 1.0%, prior 0.8%) and 3.7% y/y (expected 3.6%, prior 3.6%). Q3 headline CPI rose 1.3% q/q, above the 1.2% forecast and up from 0.6%. September CPI rose 0.8% m/m (expected 0.7%) and 4.3% y/y (expected 4.2%, prior 4.0%). The monthly trimmed mean rose 0.3% m/m and held at 3.6% y/y, both in line with forecasts. The Q3 weighted median rose 1.0% q/q, slightly below the 1.1% forecast, and 3.6% y/y. The data came as Bullock said inflation will likely exceed the RBA's August forecasts.

title: RBA's Bullock: oil shock means inflation above August forecasts, Board meets next week
body: Oil leads the hawkish read. Bullock tied the deterioration in the inflation outlook directly to re-escalating Middle East conflict and higher energy prices, so further gains in crude feed straight into the case for another RBA hike. By saying inflation will likely exceed the August base case, and asking openly whether current tightening is enough, she leaves the November 2 and 3 meeting live and supports the Australian dollar and front-end yields. Her view that the labour market is tighter than judged, despite unemployment rising, weakens the dovish argument that slowing growth will do the work. Today's quarterly trimmed mean now becomes the decisive test: a firm print would likely push markets further toward a November hike. --- Ahead: Australia CPI preview: banks see 1.0% core rise, above the RBA's 0.8% forecast Economic and event calendar in Asia Wednesday, October 28, 2026. AUD CPI, RBA and RBNZ Australia CPI explained: why 2 inflation readings land today and which one the RBA watches --- Bullock told senators that oil, AI-driven cost pressures and a tighter-than-thought labour market have pushed inflation above the RBA's August track, making next week's meeting a genuine question of whether 100bp of hikes is enough. Summary: RBA Governor Michele Bullock said inflation will likely be higher than the RBA's August base case, as some of the upside risks it flagged have materialised.

title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6734 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

title: HBM explained: the AI memory behind SK Hynix's record profits and rising chip prices
body: HBM helps explain why the memory upcycle has been so strong. Because it absorbs production capacity, AI demand lifts prices across the whole DRAM market, not just at the high end, which supports earnings at SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron and weighs on margins for PC, phone and server makers that buy memory. The concentration of supply makes the Kospi and the wider Korean market unusually sensitive to AI spending, and changes in HBM market share between SK Hynix and Samsung can move both stocks sharply. The main risk is the cycle turning: if new capacity and three-way competition in HBM4 catch up with demand, pricing power could fade quickly, as it has in past memory cycles. --- Earlier, stunning results: SK Hynix Q3 operating profit beats at 83tn won, unveils 100tn won shareholder payout plan --- HBM is the memory that keeps AI chips fed with data, and because it eats so much production capacity, it is pushing up prices for nearly every memory chip in the world. Summary: HBM stacks thin DRAM dies vertically and places them right next to the processor, delivering much higher bandwidth with less power. AI chips are often limited by how fast they can be fed data, so every leading AI accelerator, including Nvidia's GPUs, uses HBM. HBM uses around three times the wafer capacity per bit of standard DRAM, by industry estimates, so shifting production to it squeezes supply of ordinary memory and lifts prices. Only SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron make it at scale.

title: SK Hynix Q3 operating profit beats at 83tn won, unveils 100tn won shareholder payout plan
body: The operating beat and a shareholder return of about 100 trillion won give the stock strong support, and the buyback and cancellation of more than 60 trillion won stands out as a structural tailwind for SK Hynix shares and the Kospi, where it is a heavyweight. The net profit miss is the main source of headline risk until the cause is clear. The price data is the bigger signal for the sector: DRAM up by a high-20% rate in a single quarter, together with a 2027 demand outlook of around 25% growth, supports the memory upcycle for Samsung Electronics and Micron. It also confirms that AI infrastructure spending is still feeding through to component costs, which matters for hyperscaler capex budgets and the heavy AI-related debt issuance flagged by Fitch and S&P this week. --- --- Soaring memory prices drove an operating profit beat at SK Hynix, and the chipmaker is handing back about 100 trillion won to shareholders this year, even as net profit came in well short. Summary: SK Hynix Q3 operating profit was around 83 trillion won, beating the LSEG SmartEstimate of around 77 trillion won. Revenue was around 105 trillion won against around 98 trillion expected. Net profit was around 40 trillion won, well below the estimate of around 55 trillion won. DRAM average selling prices rose by a high-20% rate from Q2, and NAND prices by a mid-20% rate.

title: Australia CPI explained: why 2 inflation readings land today and which one the RBA watches
body: For the Australian dollar and front-end yields, the reaction is likely to hinge on the quarterly trimmed mean, not the headline monthly print. A reading at or above the expected 1.0% in the quarter would run ahead of the pace implied by the RBA's August forecasts and strengthen the case for a hike at the November 2 and 3 meeting. A softer core reading would give the RBA room to wait, even if fuel-driven headline inflation runs hot. A gap between the monthly and quarterly headline figures can trigger an early reaction that later reverses, as traders look past the headline to the core numbers. Oil remains the main driver of headline inflation, so energy prices will shape how hot the monthly figure runs in the months ahead. --- Earlier: Australia CPI preview: banks see 1.0% core rise, above the RBA's 0.8% forecast Economic and event calendar in Asia Wednesday, October 28, 2026. AUD CPI, RBA and RBNZ --- Australia's monthly CPI now sets the headline, but the quarterly trimmed mean is still the number the RBA trusts most, and that makes it today's main event. Summary: Both the September monthly CPI and the September quarter CPI are due at 00:30 GMT (20:30 US Eastern on Tuesday, 11:30 Sydney). Since November 2025, the ABS has published a complete monthly CPI covering most of the basket every month, replacing the partial Monthly CPI Indicator. The monthly CPI is now the headline inflation measure and the benchmark for the RBA's 2% to 3% target.

title: BlackRock sees one more Fed hike this year, calls market pricing for more too hawkish
body: BlackRock's view supports the front end of the Treasury curve. If the Fed sounds less aggressive than markets fear this week, two-year yields have the most room to fall, which would steepen the curve. Its caution on the long end, where it still sees yields rising as competition for capital intensifies, matches the heavy-supply theme flagged this week by Fitch and S&P. Neutral positioning on US equities, with a continued tilt to AI and tech, suggests BlackRock expects volatility around policy, not a broad selloff. A dovish-leaning Fed would also cap the dollar. Higher oil remains the main risk to the "less hawkish than priced" view, since further energy-driven inflation would test it. --- Earlier: FOMC Preview: A hawkish hold as markets watch for signals about timing and extent of further tightening --- BlackRock thinks the Fed will hike once more and then stop, and it is positioning for that by owning short-dated Treasuries while staying wary of long bonds. Summary: BlackRock expects one more Fed rate hike by year-end but sees market pricing for further tightening as overly hawkish. It says the recent tightening is not the start of a new, sustained hiking cycle, even after a hotter September CPI showed broadening price pressures. Markets have partly scaled back hike expectations since the September meeting, moving closer to BlackRock's view. BlackRock is overweight short-dated US Treasuries, favouring the front end for income and a greater breakeven buffer.

title: MUFG sees RBNZ hiking to 3% today but under-delivering on pricing, flags NZD downside
body: MUFG's call puts the risk squarely on the New Zealand dollar: with a hike almost fully priced, the currency's G10 outperformance this month depends on the RBNZ endorsing a much steeper path than MUFG expects. Neutral or "wait and see" language could trigger a repricing of the roughly three and a half further hikes priced, pulling front-end yields lower and weighing on the kiwi, with AUD/NZD a likely beneficiary ahead of the RBA meeting on November 2 and 3. A hawkish surprise would delay that repricing, not prevent it, in MUFG's view. Oil remains the main counterweight: further gains in crude would push up New Zealand's fuel-driven inflation and make the market's more aggressive path harder to unwind. --- Earlier: All 5 major NZ banks expect RBNZ to hike to 3% today, but split on how far rates will go Preview: RBNZ set to lift OCR to 3% ahead of election as oil and weak kiwi fuel inflation NZIER Shadow Board majority backs 25bp RBNZ hike to 3% as oil and weaker kiwi bite --- MUFG thinks the RBNZ will hike today and then disappoint, arguing that New Zealand's spare capacity cannot justify the rate path markets have priced, which leaves the kiwi's recent strength on borrowed time. Summary: MUFG expects the RBNZ to raise the OCR 25bp to 3% at 01:00 GMT (21:00 US Eastern on Tuesday), with the hike almost fully priced. It sees only one further hike, to a peak of 3.25%, while markets price around three and a half more hikes after today.

title: All 5 major NZ banks expect RBNZ to hike to 3% today, but split on how far rates will go
body: A 25bp hike is close to fully priced, so the New Zealand dollar is likely to trade on guidance, not the move itself. Language that leaves the door open to more tightening would back the hawkish paths from ASB and Westpac and lift front-end yields. "Wait and see" wording, as Kiwibank expects, would favour ANZ's pause view and could pull back some of the pricing for a peak. A split vote would add volatility either way. Oil is the swing factor beyond today: further gains in crude would add to New Zealand's fuel-driven inflation and strengthen the case for 3.5% or higher. AUD/NZD traders face back-to-back central bank risk, with the RBA meeting on November 2 and 3. --- Earlier: Preview: RBNZ set to lift OCR to 3% ahead of election as oil and weak kiwi fuel inflation NZIER Shadow Board majority backs 25bp RBNZ hike to 3% as oil and weaker kiwi bite Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Breman --- New Zealand's banks are united on a hike to 3% today, but their paths after that range from an ANZ pause to a Westpac peak of 4%, so the RBNZ's guidance matters more than the move. Summary: ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac and Kiwibank all expect the RBNZ to raise the OCR 25bp to 3% at 01:00 GMT (21:00 US Eastern on Tuesday), a third consecutive hike. Markets price roughly 90% odds of a hike. Westpac switched from a pause call after last week's CPI data. ANZ pencils in a December pause. ASB expects 3.5% by February. Westpac sees 3.5% by February and a 4% peak in September 2027.

title: Bessent says SEC and CFTC can fill the Clarity Act gap, but agency rules come with an expiry risk
body: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Washington can still deliver crypto rules without Congress. Speaking at Ripple's Swell conference, he said the Senate's failure to pass the Clarity Act was disappointing, but that Treasury would use its convening power to push a regulatory framework forward through agency action with the SEC and CFTC. The catch for investors is durability: rules written by regulators can be rewritten by the next set of regulators. What happened Bessent described the SEC and CFTC as "great partners" in the effort. He also raised debanking, the practice of financial institutions cutting off services to crypto businesses, sometimes allegedly under regulatory pressure. He said the Clarity Act could have prevented a repeat of that, but that regulatory best practices and protections can still reduce the risk. He also argued that stablecoins will lift demand for the US dollar and Treasuries, making them an important funding source for the government. The backdrop is the Senate vote six weeks ago. The Clarity Act failed to advance on September 15 on a 49-50 vote, 11 short of the 60 needed. Because the vote was procedural, the bill was never debated or amended. The two disputes that sank it were ethics rules covering officials' digital asset holdings and whether stablecoin issuers can offer yield or rewards. Why it matters The bill would have settled the question that has dogged US crypto for years: which regulator is responsible for which tokens.

title: UBS sees Brent near $110 by year-end, lifts 2027 forecasts on freight and supply risks
body: UBS is arguing that the oil market's tightness has moved from production to logistics. Even with Gulf flows close to pre-conflict levels, shipping attacks and scarce tankers keep delivered crude expensive, which means a supply recovery alone may not bring prices down much. With strategic reserve releases largely done and Chinese buying back, the market has lost two of its main shock absorbers, leaving it more exposed to any new disruption around Hormuz. Higher-for-longer oil also keeps inflation pressure in play ahead of the Fed decision, adding to the case for further tightening and weighing on rate-sensitive assets. Freight-sensitive refiners and importers in Asia are the most exposed to the shift from barrel scarcity to shipping scarcity. --- Earlier: Oil: Private survey of inventory shows a headline crude oil draw vs build expected --- Gulf oil is flowing again, but UBS says record attacks on shipping, drained inventories and returning Chinese demand mean the barrels are getting more expensive to move, keeping Brent elevated well into 2027. Summary: UBS expects Brent to hold near $110 by year-end and raised its 2027 forecasts: March to $95 from $90, June to $90 from $85 and September to $85 from $80. Global inventories have fallen sharply and pledged strategic reserve releases are largely complete, which UBS says should support prices.

title: HSBC shares slide almost 7% as revenue misses and wealth stalls despite 32% profit jump
body: The sell-off shows how much was already priced into HSBC after a strong run. Without a guidance upgrade, a revenue miss and stalled wealth growth were enough to trigger profit-taking. The read-across for Hong Kong and Asian banks is margin pressure: costlier time deposits threaten interest income just as the Fed's hiking path keeps funding costs high. Oil matters indirectly, since inflation and rate uncertainty linked to the Iran war is weighing on bank valuations broadly, and HSBC is already setting aside provisions for the Middle East conflict. The Basel 3.1 capital boost from January 2027 gives HSBC room to expand buybacks, which could limit further downside once the disappointment fades. --- Earlier: Goldman: Markets selling US banks on higher rates, but income guidance rises into 2027 --- HSBC delivered a big profit jump and another $1 billion buyback, but a revenue miss, flat wealth income and no upgrade to its targets were enough to send the shares sharply lower. Summary: HSBC shares fell almost 7% on Tuesday after third-quarter revenue of around $18.6 billion missed forecasts of roughly $19.1 billion, and adjusted EPS of $2.10 missed $2.22. Pre-tax profit rose 32% to around $9.6 billion, helped by the absence of last year's legal provisions. Excluding notable items, it rose about 10% to around $10 billion. Wealth revenue was flat at around $2.7 billion after strong growth in the first half. Net interest income rose 6% but was slightly below expectations.
